questions.question: Explain where gunpowder was invented and how it helped European explorers.
questions.expected_answer: Gunpowder, a mixture of saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur, was invented in China, probably around the ninth century AD, and was first used for fireworks and signals. Knowledge of it spread along trade routes and reached Europe by about the 1200s. By the 1400s, Portuguese ships carried cannons, which gave them power in sea battles and attacks on coastal towns and helped them force their way into trade networks.

questions.question: How did the magnetic compass and the astrolabe help sailors?
questions.expected_answer: The magnetic compass, first used for navigation in China, has a needle that points roughly north, so sailors could keep a steady direction even on cloudy days and nights. The astrolabe, developed by Greek scholars and improved in the Arab world, measured the height of the sun or stars above the horizon, so sailors could calculate their latitude.

questions.question: Describe the caravel and explain why it was good for exploration.
questions.expected_answer: The caravel was a small, light, fast Portuguese ship of the 1400s. Its triangular lateen sails, borrowed from Arab dhows and Mediterranean ships, let it sail closer into the wind. It sat high in the water, so it could explore coasts, bays and rivers, it had a rudder at the back for easier steering and it needed only a few dozen sailors. Dias used caravels to sail around southern Africa.
